newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia, Russia condemn Abkhazia vote.
newsitem.headline: Georgia, Russia condemn Abkhazia vote.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze on Monday condemned parliamentary elections in the breakaway region of Abkhazia at the weekend as a "serious mistake".
Russia backed him, saying the vote would not further peace in the republic.
"The elections...were a political farce," Shevardnadze said in a regular radio address. "The results...are pure fantasy."

The vote for a 35-member parliament, organised by Abkhazia's separatist leadership, went ahead on Saturday despite sporadic explosions from landmines along the region's de facto frontier with the rest of Georgia.
Abkhaz leaders blamed the Georgian authorities, but they denied involvment.

The Tbilisi government lost control over Abkhazia, a lush region on the Black Sea, in 1993 after a year-long war in which Georgia's disorganised armed forces waged a losing battle against Abkhaz fighters, who received military help from Russia.
The administration staged a parallel plebiscite on Saturday among Georgian refugees from the conflict and Shevardnadze said they had made their opposition to the election clear.

"Over 99 percent of the plebiscite participants said 'no' to elections in Abkhazia. They expressed their firm desire to return home and reminded the world that they would never be reconciled with the ethnic cleansing," he said.
"The falsified election in Abkhazia is a serious mistake. All international organisations called it illegal and a crude violation of democracy," said Shevardnadze, a former Soviet foreign minister.
Moscow, which now backs Georgia and has joined in a partial blockade on Abkhazia, said on Monday the election went against world opinion.
The United Nations and the European Union had pressed Abkhazia to call off the vote, saying it could fuel violence in the republic.

"This action by the Abkhaz side violates general norms, human rights and basic freedoms and completely ignores international opinion," a Russian Foreign Ministry statement, carried by Interfax news agency, said.

Abkhazia's self-declared president Vladislav Ardzinba has hailed the parliamentary vote as "the first democratic elections in Abkhazia", which he said would "facilitate the peace process" with Georgia.
But the Russian Foreign Ministry statement said the poll could only hamper the search for peace.
Russian peacekeepers now patrol the volatile border area along with U.N. military observers and Moscow said it was prepared to continue mediating the peace process.

Georgia, despite having little or no influence over the subtropical Black Sea region for the past three years, says Abkhazia can never have the independence it demands and is offering only a form of autonomy.

Some 10,000 people died in the war, which began when Georgian troops put down a drive for more autonomy. Ethnic Georgians once accounted for about 45 percent of the population but most fled during the war, fearing reprisals.
Ardzinba has indicated he will not contemplate allowing some 150,000 refugees to return to Abkhazia until the blockade is lifted.

The Abkhaz central elections commission said more than 80 percent of the 219,000-strong electorate had turned out and 30 of the 35 seats had been filled in the first round. Five run-off contests will be held in a fortnight.
Electoral officials in Tbilisi said some 230,000 refugees took part in the parallel referendum in Georgia. Only 70 said they approved the holding of the Abkhaz elections.
